correctness.rationale: For consistent rows, each delivered projection multiplies the error by I−aaᵀ. Conditioning backwards across independent deliveries gives the nested expected-energy map H↦(1−p)H+pPHP, so the objective is the largest eigenvalue of a positive semidefinite matrix, with maximization after expectation. Reflection pairs up the six orders. The exact reconstruction confirms equal traces for central-last and central-first, with determinant difference 54p³(p−2)(p−1)(36p−100)/100000<0 for 0<p<1; this strictly excludes central-last there. A common eigenvalue of central-first and central-middle is forced by subtracting their characteristic equations, and substitution yields the stated quintic times (1−p)/250000. The transformed quintic has exactly one Descartes sign change; exact opposite signs at 7/8 and 9/10 establish existence and uniqueness. The forced eigenvalue is strictly above both half-traces throughout that bracket (the two excesses decrease there and are positive at 9/10), so the common root is on both upper branches. The comparison at 1/2 and the perfect-delivery factors 1/100 versus 8/125 orient the two intervals; at p=1 the common zero eigenvalue is irrelevant and central-last loses, and at p=0 all six are identity. The exact root isolation and decimal 0.8823801245146625… agree with the frozen result.

value.rationale: Equal-budget fixed sweeps are a natural comparison in a setting where attempted but missed updates still count. The exact example shows that the best deterministic order need not even remain minimax as reliability decreases, and separates central-last from central-first despite their equality at perfect delivery. The complete threshold, tie cases and exclusion result make a reproducible benchmark for the interaction of noncommuting projections and independent omissions, beyond the observation that order sometimes matters.
residual_risks: The value is as a sharp planar benchmark, not a universal prescription for noisy or distributed solvers.
